step: Register vacancy in Central Employee Card Registry (CEVPM)
authority: Úřad práce ČR (Labour Office of the Czech Republic)
form_name: Volné pracovní místo obsaditelné držitelem zaměstnanecké karty
field_label: Vacancy notification — Employee Card eligible position
deadline_label: Minimum 30-day listing period required; begin at least 90 days before intended employment start
non_obvious_official_guidance: Before a foreign national can apply for an Employee Card, the employer must register the specific vacancy with their regional Úřad práce branch so it appears in the Central Registry of Vacancies Available to Employee Card Holders (CEVPM).
non_obvious_actual_reality: The 30-day vacancy listing period is counted separately from the embassy's up-to-60-day processing time, making the total employer-initiated lead time roughly 90 days before the employee can arrive. If the position is not listed in CEVPM at the time of the embassy appointment, the application is rejected with no opportunity to cure at that appointment.
non_obvious_action_required: Submit the vacancy to the locally competent Úřad práce branch approximately 90 days before the target start date and collect the CEVPM vacancy reference number to include in the employee's embassy application packet.
source: Zákon č. 435/2004 Sb. o zaměstnanosti §37; Ministerstvo práce a sociálních věcí

step: Obtain apostilled criminal record extract for Employee Card application
authority: Home-country law enforcement authority; Czech Embassy or Consulate
field_label: Criminal record extract — Employee Card supporting document
deadline_label: Document must be no older than 6 months at the date of the embassy appointment
non_obvious_official_guidance: Employee Card applicants must provide a criminal record certificate from their country of citizenship and from every other country in which they resided for 6 or more months in the past 3 years, each apostilled and translated into Czech.
non_obvious_actual_reality: In many countries the official criminal record extract takes 4–6 weeks and then requires a further apostille; applicants who have lived in multiple countries must collect multiple documents, each apostilled separately. The document is valid for only 6 months, so obtaining it too early means it expires before the appointment — timing against the embassy booking window is critical.
non_obvious_action_required: Request all required extracts and apostilles at least 8 weeks before the embassy appointment date. Arrange certified Czech translations for each. Verify the Czech embassy's specific translation and legalisation requirements in the country of application, as requirements vary by post.
source: Zákon č. 326/1999 Sb. §31 odst. 1 písm. e); MV ČR Employee Card requirements

step: Apply for Employee Card (zaměstnanecká karta) at Czech Embassy
authority: Czech Embassy or Consulate; Ministry of the Interior — OAMP (MV ČR)
form_name: Žádost o povolení k dlouhodobému pobytu — zaměstnanecká karta
field_label: Application for long-term residence permit — Employee Card
deadline_label: Standard processing up to 60 days; apply at least 60 days before intended arrival
non_obvious_official_guidance: The Employee Card is a combined work and residence permit applied for in person at the Czech Embassy in the applicant's country of legal residence; it is issued by MV ČR and is valid for the duration of the employment contract plus 3 months, up to a maximum of 2 years.
non_obvious_actual_reality: Embassy appointment slots in some countries are fully booked 4–6 weeks in advance; the employee must appear in person and the application must reference the specific CEVPM vacancy ID provided by the employer. The employer's signed employment contract must accompany the application even before the employee has started work, which some HR teams are reluctant to provide pre-arrival.
non_obvious_action_required: Book the embassy appointment as soon as the CEVPM vacancy reference number is available. Bring: passport valid at least 3 months beyond the intended stay, CEVPM vacancy reference, signed employment contract, proof of Czech accommodation, passport photo, apostilled criminal record extract, and proof of health insurance or capacity to obtain it. Pay the consular fee.

step: Apply for family reunification long-term residence permit for dependants
authority: Czech Embassy or Consulate; MV ČR — OAMP
form_name: Žádost o povolení k dlouhodobému pobytu za účelem sloučení rodiny
field_label: Family reunification long-term residence permit — dependant
deadline_label: Apply only after the primary Employee Card has been issued; allow minimum 60 days processing
non_obvious_official_guidance: Dependant family members of Employee Card holders may apply for a family reunification long-term residence permit; standard processing takes up to 270 days for initial applications, though typically 60–90 days in practice.
non_obvious_actual_reality: Dependants cannot apply simultaneously with the primary holder — the Employee Card must first be issued and presented as evidence. This structural sequencing means the primary holder often needs to travel and begin work several months before the family can join. School enrolment for minor children requires a confirmed Czech address and a valid residence document, so the gap can disrupt school-year planning significantly.
non_obvious_action_required: File the primary Employee Card application as early as possible to start the clock. Once the Employee Card is issued, immediately file dependant applications at the Czech Embassy. Contact the destination municipality's school registration office in advance to understand documentation requirements and registration deadlines.

step: Report place of residence to Foreign Police within 3 working days of entry
authority: Cizinecká policie — Ředitelství služby cizinecké policie
field_label: Address registration obligation on entry — non-EU nationals
deadline_label: Within 3 working days of entry into Czech Republic
non_obvious_official_guidance: Foreign nationals holding a long-term visa or residence permit must report their place of residence to the Foreign Police within 3 working days of entry into the Czech Republic.
non_obvious_actual_reality: Hotels and licensed accommodation providers fulfil this obligation automatically on check-in. In a private apartment, the employee must attend the locally competent Cizinecká policie office in person — some landlords are reluctant to provide the written address confirmation (prohlášení o ubytování) required, and the office visit can take several hours with no appointment system at many branches.
non_obvious_action_required: If in private accommodation: visit the nearest Cizinecká policie office with passport, Employee Card visa sticker, and a signed landlord address declaration. Confirm office opening hours before attending as many branches operate reduced or appointment-only windows. Arrange the landlord declaration before arrival day.
source: Zákon č. 326/1999 Sb. §93 odst. 1; MV ČR

step: Submit biometric data at MV ČR OAMP office to initiate Employee Card production
authority: Ministerstvo vnitra — OAMP (Department for Asylum and Migration Policy)
field_label: Biometric data submission — Employee Card production appointment
deadline_label: Within 3 working days of arrival; appointment must be booked before travel
non_obvious_official_guidance: After entering the Czech Republic on the Employee Card visa sticker, the holder must attend the designated MV ČR OAMP workplace within 3 working days to have biometric data (fingerprints and photograph) recorded for production of the biometric residence card.
non_obvious_actual_reality: The visa sticker in the passport is a temporary travel document, not the final permit. Failure to attend the biometric appointment within 3 working days can result in the permit being voided. MV ČR OAMP appointment slots at Prague offices fill weeks in advance and must be booked online through the MV ČR portal before the employee departs from their home country.
non_obvious_action_required: Book the biometric appointment at an MV ČR OAMP workplace via the MV ČR online booking system before purchasing travel. Bring: original passport with visa sticker, one biometric passport photo, and proof of Czech residential address. The physical card is typically ready for collection 2–4 weeks later.
source: Zákon č. 326/1999 Sb. §44a; MV ČR Employee Card guidance

step: Register EU/EEA/Swiss national temporary residence with MV ČR or Foreign Police
authority: Ministerstvo vnitra — OAMP or Cizinecká policie
form_name: Přihláška k přechodnému pobytu občana EU na území ČR
deadline_label: Required for stays exceeding 30 days; register within 30 days of arrival
non_obvious_official_guidance: EU/EEA/Swiss nationals exercising free movement rights may reside in the Czech Republic for up to 30 days without registration; for longer stays they must register their temporary residence and receive a confirmation certificate (potvrzení o přechodném pobytu).
non_obvious_actual_reality: Registration is not a legal condition of the right to reside under EU free movement, but without the confirmation certificate it is practically impossible to open a Czech bank account, enrol with a general practitioner, or be registered for health insurance as a self-payer. Many HR onboarding checklists incorrectly treat EU nationals as needing no Czech paperwork at all.
non_obvious_action_required: Visit the MV ČR OAMP or Cizinecká policie office within 30 days of arrival. Bring: national ID card or passport, employment contract or proof of economic activity in Czech Republic, and proof of Czech residential address (lease or employer accommodation letter). The certificate is issued free of charge on the same visit.
source: Zákon č. 326/1999 Sb. §87a; MV ČR — EU citizens residence

step: Employer registers employee with statutory health insurer (VZP or chosen company)
authority: VZP ČR or chosen statutory health insurance company
form_name: Oznámení o nástupu zaměstnance do zaměstnání — přihláška pojištěnce
field_label: Employee enrolment notification — public health insurance
deadline_label: Within 8 calendar days of employment commencement
source: Zákon č. 48/1997 Sb. o veřejném zdravotním pojištění §8; VZP ČR

step: Employer registers employee with ČSSZ (Czech Social Security Administration)
deadline_label: Within 8 calendar days of employment commencement
source: Zákon č. 582/1991 Sb. o organizaci a provádění sociálního zabezpečení §§93–94; ČSSZ

step: Employer notifies Úřad práce of non-EU national commencing work
authority: Úřad práce ČR — locally competent branch
form_name: Oznámení o nástupu cizince k výkonu práce na území ČR
field_label: Foreign national employment commencement notification — Labour Office
deadline_label: Within 10 calendar days of employment commencement
non_obvious_official_guidance: Under the Employment Act, employers must notify the locally competent Labour Office branch whenever a non-EU/EEA foreign national begins, terminates, or changes employment in the Czech Republic.
non_obvious_actual_reality: This Labour Office notification is a wholly separate obligation from the pre-arrival CEVPM vacancy registration and from the 8-day ČSSZ and health insurer registrations — three parallel filings to three different bodies, all within the first two weeks. The notification must go to the Úřad práce branch in whose district the employee's actual workplace sits, not the employer's registered office. Fines for non-notification reach CZK 2,000,000.
non_obvious_action_required: Submit the commencement notification — and separately a termination notification when employment ends — to the Úřad práce branch covering the physical work location. Retain a copy with the personnel file as audit evidence for inspection.
source: Zákon č. 435/2004 Sb. o zaměstnanosti §87; MPSV

step: Confirm rodné číslo (Czech personal identification number) and provide to employer payroll
field_label: Rodné číslo — Czech personal identification number
deadline_label: Typically assigned when biometric Employee Card is issued; confirm and provide within 30 days of arrival
non_obvious_official_guidance: A rodné číslo (birth number) is the primary personal identifier used for tax, social security, and health insurance purposes in Czech Republic; it is assigned to registered foreign residents by MV ČR and is printed on the biometric Employee Card.
non_obvious_actual_reality: The rodné číslo is only physically visible once the biometric card is collected, which can be 2–4 weeks after the biometric appointment. Running payroll without a valid rodné číslo causes ČSSZ electronic submissions (ELDP) to fail and requires retroactive manual correction. EU nationals who do not automatically receive a rodné číslo should proactively request one from MV ČR OAMP after their residence registration.
non_obvious_action_required: As soon as the biometric Employee Card is collected, provide the rodné číslo to the employer's payroll team. If the card is delayed beyond 3 weeks, contact MV ČR OAMP to obtain the number directly and confirm it before the first payroll run.
source: Zákon č. 133/2000 Sb. o evidenci obyvatel §§16a–17a; MV ČR

step: Register with Finanční správa for personal income tax
form_name: Přihláška k registraci pro fyzické osoby (tiskopis MFin 5405)
field_label: Personal income tax registration — physical person
deadline_label: Within 30 days of receiving first Czech-sourced taxable income
source: Zákon č. 280/2009 Sb. (Daňový řád) §125 odst. 1; Finanční správa ČR

step: Employer remits monthly payroll tax withholding and social/health contributions
authority: Finanční správa ČR; ČSSZ; statutory health insurer
form_name: Přiznání k záloze na daň z příjmů fyzických osob ze závislé činnosti
field_label: Monthly PAYE withholding and contributions remittance
deadline_label: By the 20th of the month following the payroll month
source: Zákon č. 586/1992 Sb. §38h; Zákon č. 589/1992 Sb.; Zákon č. 48/1997 Sb.; Finanční správa ČR

step: Determine applicable social security legislation and obtain A1 or bilateral agreement certificate
authority: ČSSZ (EU cases); home-country social security authority; bilateral treaty counterpart authority
form_name: A1 certificate (EU/EEA/CH secondees); bilateral portability certificate (treaty countries)
field_label: Social security legislation applicability — EU Regulation 883/2004 or bilateral treaty
deadline_label: Must be determined before employment begins; A1 or treaty certificate must be in place from day 1
non_obvious_official_guidance: Under EU Regulation 883/2004, only one member state's social security legislation applies at a time. Czech Republic also has bilateral social security agreements with Ukraine, India, South Korea, Japan, Canada, the USA, Serbia, Montenegro, North Macedonia, and Turkey among others.
non_obvious_actual_reality: EU nationals seconded from another EU country without a valid A1 certificate must pay full Czech social security contributions (employer 24.8%, employee 6.5%) regardless of concurrent contributions made in their home state, creating double liability. Non-EU nationals from non-treaty countries face the same full Czech liability with no offset for contributions paid elsewhere. Many employers only discover the double-liability exposure at year-end audit.
non_obvious_action_required: EU/EEA/Swiss nationals on secondment: employer must obtain A1 certificate from the home-state social security authority before employment begins in Czech Republic. Non-EU nationals: verify bilateral treaty scope with ČSSZ and plan payroll cost accordingly. Engage a social security specialist where totalization or detachment rules are unclear.
source: Nařízení (ES) č. 883/2004; Zákon č. 187/2006 Sb.; ČSSZ — international

step: Assess permanent establishment (PE) risk for foreign employer with employee based in Czech Republic
field_label: Permanent establishment risk — foreign entity, Czech-based employee
deadline_label: Assess from day 1 of employee working in Czech Republic
non_obvious_official_guidance: Under Czech Income Tax Act §22 and applicable double tax treaties, a foreign company may create a taxable permanent establishment in Czech Republic through a fixed place of business or through an employee habitually exercising authority to conclude contracts on behalf of the foreign enterprise.
non_obvious_actual_reality: Home-office and remote-working arrangements are a high-risk area: if the employee regularly works from a Czech address that effectively constitutes the foreign company's place of business, Finanční správa may deem a PE to exist. The risk is compounded where the employee has discretion to bind the employer contractually. A PE triggers Czech corporate income tax registration, filing, and potentially VAT registration obligations for the foreign entity.
non_obvious_action_required: Foreign employers should commission a Czech PE risk opinion from a qualified tax advisor before the employee starts work. Employment contracts should clearly define scope and explicitly exclude authority to conclude contracts in the employer's name. Shadow payroll implications should be assessed concurrently.
source: Zákon č. 586/1992 Sb. §22; Modelová smlouva OECD; Finanční správa ČR — mezinárodní zdanění

step: Monitor days in Czech Republic to assess tax residence under 183-day rule
field_label: Tax residence determination — worldwide income exposure
deadline_label: Tax residence crystallises when domicile is established or 183 days in a calendar year are reached
non_obvious_official_guidance: A foreign national becomes a Czech tax resident if they have a domicile (permanent home) in Czech Republic or habitually reside there for 183 or more days in a calendar year, triggering Czech income tax liability on worldwide income.
non_obvious_actual_reality: The 183-day count includes both the arrival and departure day and is assessed per calendar year (1 January–31 December), not on a rolling 12-month basis. An employee arriving in late July can become a Czech tax resident before the end of their first calendar year faster than expected, simultaneously exposing overseas rental income, foreign dividends, and foreign bank interest to Czech taxation.
non_obvious_action_required: Track days physically present in Czech Republic from the date of arrival. If approaching 183 days in the calendar year, consult a Czech tax advisor before the threshold is crossed to assess whether an applicable double tax treaty preserves non-resident status and whether home-country tax residency can be maintained. Do not rely solely on the employer's payroll team — this is a personal filing obligation.
source: Zákon č. 586/1992 Sb. §2 odst. 2–4; Finanční správa ČR — mezinárodní zdanění

step: File annual personal income tax return (daňové přiznání k dani z příjmů)
authority: Finanční správa ČR — locally competent tax office
form_name: Daňové přiznání k dani z příjmů fyzických osob (tiskopis MFin 5405)
field_label: Annual personal income tax return — physical person
deadline_label: 1 April (paper or electronic); 1 May (electronic self-filed extension); 1 July (with registered tax advisor mandate)
non_obvious_official_guidance: Employees whose sole Czech income comes from one employer with payroll tax correctly withheld may request the employer to carry out the annual tax settlement (roční zúčtování) instead of filing independently; the request deadline is 15 February following the tax year.
non_obvious_actual_reality: Foreign employees with any overseas income (rental, dividends, foreign salary, foreign bank interest) or who are Czech tax residents in their first partial year must file independently even if Czech PAYE was correctly withheld all year. The 23% higher rate band applies to gross income above CZK 1,582,812 (2024 threshold — confirm annually). Filing jointly with a Czech-resident spouse can materially reduce liability.
non_obvious_action_required: By January each year, assess with a Czech tax advisor whether an independent filing obligation exists based on your global income profile. If filing independently, collect: employer annual wage certificate (potvrzení o zdanitelných příjmech ze závislé činnosti), foreign bank statements, and documentation of any overseas income. Submit electronically where possible.
source: Zákon č. 586/1992 Sb. §38g–38i; Finanční správa ČR

step: Apply to renew Employee Card before expiry
form_name: Žádost o prodloužení doby platnosti povolení k dlouhodobému pobytu
deadline_label: Apply no earlier than 90 days and no later than before the expiry date; do not allow card to lapse
non_obvious_official_guidance: Employee Card holders must apply for renewal in person at an MV ČR OAMP office; the renewal window opens exactly 90 days before expiry and the application must be submitted before expiry to maintain the uninterrupted legal right to work.
non_obvious_actual_reality: Applications submitted more than 90 days before expiry are inadmissible and returned without processing. Applications submitted after expiry cause the employee to lose the legal right to work immediately with no grace period. Employment contracts are frequently extended by informal email without triggering a card renewal — the card expiry date and the extended contract end date drift apart silently, and HR teams rarely flag this.
non_obvious_action_required: Set a calendar alert 100 days before the card expiry date. Book an MV ČR OAMP appointment at the 90-day mark — slots at Prague offices are scarce and must be booked online in advance. Before the appointment, confirm in writing that the employment contract has been formally extended and obtain a new signed contract amendment to present at the renewal interview.
source: Zákon č. 326/1999 Sb. §44a odst. 3–4; MV ČR

step: Notify MV ČR of change of residential address within 30 days of moving
authority: Ministerstvo vnitra — OAMP or Cizinecká policie
deadline_label: Within 30 days of moving to new address
source: Zákon č. 326/1999 Sb. §93 odst. 3; MV ČR
